scope: Selected manually observed pointer selection in the isolated macOS ARM64 LibreCAD build, with a locally generated 18-vertex IMAGE.
checks: In the normal clipped drawing, clicking the visible polygon selected one IMAGE; clicking a point in the clipped-out interior of the rectangular frame selected none and began a selection window.
With inverted clipping, clicking a visible pixel selected one IMAGE and clicking the central clipped-out polygon selected none. Clicking the visible pixel again deselected it.

In the skewed output reopened from a prior native save, clicking the visible polygon selected one IMAGE; after deselection a point inside the image parallelogram but well outside the clip selected none. Clicking the image frame corner selected the image, even though that frame lay outside the visible polygon.
The application was built with a scratch-only settings organization and separate signed bundle. Inputs and raster were locally created and no drawing fixture was committed.
limits: These are selected pointer clicks, not an exhaustive selection tolerance, snapping, window/crossing selection, move/copy, undo/redo or boundary semantics check.
The image frame remains selectable even where its pixels are clipped; the selected outline follows the image parallelogram.
Other image graph profiles, independent producers, printing, Linux and Windows GUI behavior remain unqualified.
